706644.t: Folk-etymological adaptation of יְרוּשָׁלַיִם (Yərūšālayim), influenced by ἱερός (hĭerós, “sacred; holy”).

706633.t: From Proto-Hellenic *iherós, from Proto-Indo-European *ish₁rós. There are a number of candidate cognates with this word; these include Sanskrit इषिर (iṣirá, “strong, active”) and Oscan 𐌀𐌉𐌔𐌖𐌔𐌉𐌔 (aisusis, “sacrifices”).

706696.t: From Proto-Hellenic *yīyēmi, reduplicated present of Proto-Indo-European *(H)yeh₁- (“to throw”). Compare Latin iaciō, Hittite [script needed] (pe-iezzi, “sends away”).

706614.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *ihereús. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀂𐀋𐀩𐀄 (i-je-re-u).

706603.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wīrāks, from Proto-Indo-European *wiHrós (“man”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *weyh₁- (“to chase, pursue”), with possible folk-etymological influence by ἱερός (hĭerós, “holy, divine”).
